what_it_does: Quantum and probabilistic computers can solve hard optimization problems by finding the lowest-energy configuration of an Ising model (a physics concept where you minimize the sum of weighted interactions between binary variables). However, real-world problems have constraints: certain combinations of variable values are forbidden. Existing solvers handle this by adding penalty terms (extra energy costs) to discourage bad states, but this causes the solver to waste most of its compute time exploring invalid solutions. This paper proposes an encoding circuit that sits between the solver and the problem, restricting the solver to only explore legal variable assignments without any penalty terms. The Fuse software framework makes this approach practical by automatically lowering high-level constraint descriptions into encoded Ising models tailored to the target hardware (quantum, oscillator-based, or probabilistic computers).
